node.title: Re^3: Counting text with ligatures
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
My initial understanding of the OP's question was that it has to do with Unicode being able to represent the same user-visible character in multiple different ways, like with combining characters. That is, the two strings "\N{LATIN SMALL LETTER E WITH ACUTE}" and "e\N{COMBINING ACUTE ACCENT}" report different [doc://length]s (1 resp. 2), even though on the screen they both look like "é" (one "grapheme"), and so users would expect a "length" of each string to be reported as 1. I may have misunderstood the OP's question though - if you have the strings "ffi" vs. "ﬃ", and you want to know if they have the same length and/or are equal, then perhaps what the OP is looking for is [wp://Unicode equivalence] ([http://unicode.org/faq/normalization.html|normalization]).

use Unicode::Normalize; use Data::Dump; dd NFD("\N{LATIN SMALL LETTER E WITH ACUTE}"), NFD("e\N{COMBINING ACUTE ACCENT}"); dd NFC("\N{LATIN SMALL LETTER E WITH ACUTE}"), NFC("e\N{COMBINING ACUTE ACCENT}"); dd NFKD("\N{LATIN SMALL LIGATURE FFI}"); __END__ ("e\x{301}", "e\x{301}") ("\xE9", "\xE9") "ffi"

Updated example code to include the "é" examples.
